# assignmentB2LucaStoeckl

This package has one function, `count_all_missing_by_group()`. You give it a data frame and a grouping column, and it tells you how many NAs every column has in each group. I wrote this kind of `group_by()` + `summarize(across(...))` code again and again when looking at new data, so now it is one call.

## Installation

Install version 0.1.0 from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("UBC-STAT545-F2026/assignment-B2-Luca-Stoeckl", ref = "0.1.0")
```

## Usage

NAs per month in the `airquality` data:

```{r example}
library(assignmentB2LucaStoeckl)

count_all_missing_by_group(airquality, Month)
```

Almost all NAs are in `Ozone`. June alone has 21 of them, so for Ozone in June I would be careful.

Piping works too:

```{r pipe}
airquality |> count_all_missing_by_group(Month)
```

The output is ungrouped by default. With `.groups = "keep"` it stays grouped by `Month`:

```{r keep}
count_all_missing_by_group(airquality, Month, .groups = "keep")
```

Full documentation: `?count_all_missing_by_group`.
